title: Distributive conditional types and pitfalls
hook: When T in T extends U ? X : Y is a naked type parameter that is a union, the conditional distributes — it runs once per union member and unions the results. That power builds Exclude and Extract; the pitfall is surprise when you meant to test the whole union at once.

blocks.text: A **distributive conditional type** applies when **T** is a **naked type parameter** (not wrapped in tuple or object) and **T** resolves to a **union**. The compiler rewrites `T extends U ? X : Y` where `T = A | B` into `(A extends U ? X : Y) | (B extends U ? X : Y)`. **Exclude** and **Extract** rely on this. To **disable** distribution, wrap **T** as **`[T]`** in both sides: `[T] extends [U] ? X : Y` tests the union as a whole.

entries.plainDefinition: Conditional over union parameter becomes union of per-member conditionals.
entries.example: T extends string ? A : B over string|number → A|B

entries.plainDefinition: Bare T in conditional — not T & {}, not [T], not keyof T.
Tuple wrap [T] extends [U] prevents per-member split.
Output is | of each branch result — may be wider than expected.

blocks.text: Senior Reddit threads flag distributivity as the #1 conditional-type gotcha. `ToArray<T> = T extends any ? T[] : never` over `string | number` becomes `string[] | number[]` not `(string | number)[]`. Utility types Exclude/Extract filter union members — impossible without distribution. Mis-wrapping T causes subtle generic library bugs in event maps and API routers.

blocks.body: T extends any ? X : Y distributes over union members — any on the right of extends is the trick for 'map over union'.

blocks.text: Explain why Exclude works — distribution + never absorbs members. Implement UnionToIntersection trick (contravariant infer) as advanced follow-up. Read TS handbook distributive section. Production: filter union of event names with conditional never pattern. When compiler slows, simplify nested distributive maps — module 18 complexity budget.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Cannot explain Exclude via distribution. Surprised by string[] | number[]. No fix with [T] wrap. Saying distribution happens at runtime.

interviewTakeaways: Naked union type parameter distributes conditional over each member.
Exclude/Extract are distributive filters — never removes matching members.
[T] extends [U] disables distribution — test whole union.
60s: T extends U ? X : Y on T = A|B becomes (A branch)|(B branch). Exclude uses never. [T] wrap for homogenous tuple/array. Compile-time only.
commonPitfalls: Weak: surprised by string[] | number[] from ToArray
Weak: no [T] wrap when whole union needed
Strong: 'Naked T distributes. Exclude is filter. [T] disables. T extends any maps over union.'
